name: Ichthyosis hystrix of Curth-Macklin

criteria.description: Presence of extensive hyperkeratotic, spiny or verrucous plaques primarily on extensor surfaces
Diffuse or focal palmoplantar keratoderma with cobblestone-like appearance
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the KRT14 gene
Histological evidence of epidermolytic hyperkeratosis with perinuclear vacuolization
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of hyperkeratotic plaques and palmoplantar keratoderma plus identification of KRT14 mutation or compatible histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is critical for confirmation; histopathology supports diagnosis.

occasional.symptomName: Bleeding with minor or no trauma

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing epidermolytic hyperkeratosis with perinuclear vacuolization
Histopathology revealing thickened stratum corneum with hypergranulosis
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern

distinguishingFeatures: More generalized blistering and erythroderma in infancy
Mutations in KRT1 or KRT10 genes
Histology shows epidermolytic hyperkeratosis but clinical presentation differs
Generalized scaling without spiny hyperkeratotic plaques

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin fissures leading to secondary infection
Severe contractures impairing hand or foot function
Signs of systemic infection or sepsis from skin barrier breakdown
references: Curth HO, Macklin MT. Ichthyosis hystrix: a distinctive type of hereditary ichthyosis. Arch Dermatol. 1954.
